name: What is the difference between expanding a kitchen inside the home versus building an exterior bump-out?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between expanding a kitchen inside the home versus building an exterior bump-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Expanding within your existing footprint alters interior partition walls, while a bump-out addition extends the home's exterior walls outward onto a new foundation. Modifying interior space to claim an underused dining area or pantry is generally faster because the building envelope remains untouched. An exterior bump-out adds true new square footage, which is ideal when surrounding interior rooms cannot be sacrificed. However, bump-outs require excavation, concrete foundation work, roofing tie-ins, and exterior finish matching, adding construction steps.
acceptedAnswer.description: Expanding inside takes space from adjacent rooms without altering exterior walls, whereas a bump-out builds outward on a new foundation to create brand-new square footage.
